anf_compare.notes: ANF/NPNF has no text of this letter; translated directly from the PG 77 Greek.

choices.term: Περὶ τοῦ ἐπίσκοπον καθαιρεθέντα καὶ τοῦ ἱερουργεῖν παύεσθαι
choices.english: On a deposed bishop also ceasing from sacred ministry
rejected: On a bishop who has been deposed and on his ceasing from sacred ministry
That a deposed bishop must cease from sacred ministry
choices.why: The first τοῦ governs the infinitive παύεσθαι with ἐπίσκοπον καθαιρεθέντα as its subject; τοῦ ἱερουργεῖν is a genitive of separation. One topic, not two, and the heading carries no 'must'.

choices.english: moves straight along the path of canonical good order
rejected: are carried straight of canonical good order
choices.why: εὐθύ with the genitive means 'straight toward'; the English keeps the image of a straight course without a calque.

choices.term: ψῆφον ἀπροσκλινῆ, ἥ 277 περ ἂν γένοιτο περί τινων
choices.english: an impartial verdict, whomever it may concern
rejected: a vote not inclining, whichever might come about concerning some
choices.why: ἀπροσκλινής is 'not leaning to either side', i.e. impartial; the relative clause is general ('concerning any persons').

choices.term: εἴπερ ἦν ἄξιος τοῦ μὴ προεστάναι θείου θυσιαστηρίου
choices.english: if he truly deserved not to preside at the divine altar
rejected: if he was not worthy to preside at the divine altar
choices.why: The negation sits on the infinitive: he deserved removal. Moving it onto ἄξιος would change the claim.
Honorific address to Domnus; lowercase to match the neighbouring rows.

pass_a_gloss: [Latin edition title: Epistula canonica ad Domnum = canonical letter to Domnus.] Of the one among the saints Cyril, archbishop of Alexandria. Cyril to Domnus. 1 (alpha). Concerning (with articular infinitive) a bishop having been deposed (aor. pass. ptc.) and the ceasing from performing sacred rites. Each of the affairs concerning us, whenever they are carried (pres. subj. pass.) straight (with gen.) toward canonical good order, begets for us no disturbance, and frees also from the ill-speaking from some, and rather also procures for us the good-speaking from those thinking well. For who would not accept a vote/verdict not inclining (impartial), whichever might come about (opt.) concerning any persons, or how will judging rightly and lawfully not be unreprovable, but rather full of all praise? And these things I write now, your God-fearingness in its own letters, those sent to me and to the most holy and most God-beloved our brother and fellow bishop Proclus, naming as bishop the most reverent and most God-fearing Peter, while he himself is weeping and saying that from the church allotted (aor. pass. ptc.) to him he has been moved (pf. pass. inf.) unreasonably. And it was consistent: either that he have the name of the priesthood with the reality, or at least, if indeed he was worthy of not presiding (pf. inf., negated) over the divine altar, not even by the very [continues in ep-rem-early].
pass_b_english: By Saint Cyril, Archbishop of Alexandria.
1. On a deposed bishop also ceasing from sacred ministry.

When each of our affairs moves straight along the path of canonical good order, it stirs up no turmoil for us; it also frees us from the slanders of some, and, better still, wins us the good word of right-minded people. For who would not welcome an impartial verdict, whomever it may concern? Or how could judging rightly and lawfully be anything but beyond reproach, or rather full of every praise? I write this now because your piety, in the letters you sent to me and to our most holy and most God-beloved brother and fellow bishop Proclus, calls the most reverent and most God-fearing Peter a bishop, while he weeps and says that he has been removed without reason from the church assigned to him.
It would have been consistent either for him to hold the name of the priesthood together with its reality, or at least, if he truly deserved not to preside at the divine altar, not even…
source_text:
Epistula canonica ad Domnum
ΤΟΥ ΕΝ ΑΓΙΟΙΣ ΚΥΡΙΛΛΟΥ ΑΡΧΙΕΠΙΣΚΟΠΟΥ ΑΛΕΞΑΝ∆ΡΕΙΑΣ Κύριλλος
∆όμνῳ Α Περὶ τοῦ ἐπίσκοπον καθαιρεθέντα καὶ τοῦ ἱερουργεῖν
παύεσθαι.
Ἕκαστα τῶν καθ' ἡμᾶς πραγμάτων, ὅταν εὐθὺ φέρωνται κανονικῆς εὐταξίας
, οὐδένα μὲν ἡμῖν ἐντίκτει θόρυβον, ἀπαλάττει δὲ καὶ τῆς παρά τινων δυσφημίας
, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ τὰς παρὰ τῶν εὖ φρονούντων εὐφημίας ἡμῖν προξενεῖ. Τίς γὰρ οὐκ
ἂν ἀποδέξαιτο ψῆφον ἀπροσκλινῆ, ἥ 277 περ ἂν γένοιτο περί τινων, ἢ πῶς τὸ
κρίνειν ὀρθῶς καὶ ἐννόμως οὐκ ἀνεπίπληκτον ἔσται, μᾶλλον δὲ παντὸς ἐπαίνου
μεστόν; Καὶ ταῦτα γράφω νυνί, τῆς σῆς θεοσεβείας ἐν τοῖς ἑαυτῆς γράμμασι, τοῖς
σταλεῖσι πρὸς ἐμέ τε καὶ τὸν ὁσιώτατόν τε καὶ θεοφιλέστατον ἀδελφὸν ἡμῶν καὶ
συνεπίσκοπον Πρόκλον, ἐπίσκοπον μὲν ὀνομαζούσης τὸν εὐλαβέστατον καὶ
θεοσεβέστατον Πέτρον, αὐτοῦ δὲ κλαίοντος καὶ τῆς ἐκνεμηθείσης ἐκκλησίας αὐτῷ
παραλόγως κεκινῆσθαι λέγοντος.
Ἦν δ' ἀκόλουθον, ἢ τὸ τῆς ἱερωσύνης ὄνομα μετὰ τοῦ πράγματος ἔχειν
αὐτόν, ἢ γοῦν, εἴπερ ἦν ἄξιος τοῦ μὴ προεστάναι θείου θυσιαστηρίου, μηδ' αὐτῇ
source_normalizations: 'ἥ 277 περ' is ἥπερ split by the PG column number 277; the number is not text and is not translated.
The title line has ∆ (increment sign) for Δ in ΑΛΕΞΑΝ∆ΡΕΙΑΣ and ∆όμνῳ; read as Delta. The source file is left as locked.
notes: The row ends mid-sentence at μηδ' αὐτῇ; the sentence continues in ep-rem-early with τιμᾶσθαι τῇ κλήσει τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς. Pass B ends 'not even…' and ep-rem-early opens '…to be honored with the very title of bishop'.

Peter is the bishop removed from his see; Proclus is a fellow bishop to whom Domnus also wrote. Roles checked against the genitive absolute (τῆς σῆς θεοσεβείας … ὀνομαζούσης, αὐτοῦ δὲ κλαίοντος … λέγοντος).
No Scripture quoted or clearly alluded to in this row.

review.coverage: every clause checked against the source
changes: Heading 1 corrected from two topics to one: τοῦ governs παύεσθαι with ἐπίσκοπον καθαιρεθέντα as subject ('On a deposed bishop also ceasing from sacred ministry').
'whoever it may concern' corrected to 'whomever it may concern'.
Translator note addressed to another reviewer rewritten as a plain editorial note.
checked: negation on the infinitive: 'if he truly deserved not to preside at the divine altar'
agency in the genitive absolute: Domnus calls Peter a bishop; Peter weeps and complains
honorifics: 'your piety', 'most holy and most God-beloved', 'most reverent and most God-fearing'

reviewer: claude source review, separate pass (same model family as the drafter)
